chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And verily they were called upon to make obeisance while yet they were safe."

He (AS) said: "The capable are capable of fulfilling the obligations that have been imposed on them. And the capable are capable of refraining from the prohibitions that were imposed on them. They will be tried through both obligation and prohibition." Then he added, "There is nothing which has been commanded or prohibited by Allah, the Exalted, the Mighty and High, that is not a trial and predestined."
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of being called to prostration while safe in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the phrase 'while they were safe' as indicating full capability (*istita'ah*) to obey commands and avoid prohibitions, thereby establishing the condition for divine accountability. He expands this by asserting that every specific command and prohibition constitutes a distinct trial (*ibtala*) and part of divine decree (*qada*), highlighting the intricate link between human capacity and God's testing mechanism in Shia theological discourse.
